bull.b: Growing Elfabrio sales, geographic approvals, and European once-every-four-weeks approval support broader adoption of the commercial product. These developments can strengthen recurring product economics and partner demand, while expanding access in the Fabry market over the next several quarters.

The shift to positive TTM net income and strong gross and operating margins indicates meaningful operating improvement from the prior loss-making profile. If commercial revenue remains supported by Elfabrio, this profitability provides greater capacity to fund development and sustain operations.

A substantial cash position without outstanding debt or warrants gives Protalix financial flexibility to support commercial execution and advance its pipeline. The absence of debt also limits interest burden and refinancing pressure, improving resilience through clinical and partnership milestones.

bear.b: Dependence on Chiesi purchases and uneven shipment timing can make reported revenue difficult to forecast, even when underlying demand is progressing. This variability complicates planning, reduces confidence in quarterly comparisons, and leaves performance more exposed to one partner's inventory decisions.

The $25M milestone materially increased first-half revenue but is not a recurring product-sale driver. Comparisons may therefore overstate the underlying pace of commercial growth, leaving future revenue and profitability dependent on recurring Elfabrio sales and additional partner activity.

The observed anti-drug antibody rate and unresolved regimen choice create uncertainty around PRX-115's clinical development path. Immunogenicity and infusion-related reaction concerns could require dose or regimen changes, affecting development timing, eventual positioning, and the pipeline's contribution to future growth.
